_meta.indication: For the treatment of pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) who have symptomatic, inoperable plexiform neurofibromas (PN)

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase I/II (Phase II Stratum 1 was the basis for approval)
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, single-arm, multicenter trial conducted by the NCI Pediatric Oncology Branch
pivotal_trials.population: Pediatric patients 2-18 years of age with NF1 and inoperable PN causing significant morbidity
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) — percentage of patients with complete response or confirmed partial response (≥ 20% reduction in PN volume)
pivotal_trials.result: ORR per REiNS criteria was 66% (95% CI: 51, 79) by NCI central review; median DOR not reached, with 82% of responders having a DOR of at least 12 months

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥ 40%): vomiting, rash, abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, dry skin, fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, pyrexia, acneiform rash, stomatitis, headache, paronychia, pruritus. Serious adverse events occurred in 24% of patients; permanent discontinuation for AEs in 12%. Key warnings include cardiomyopathy (decreased LVEF in 23% of 74 patients) and ocular toxicity (15%)
target_moa: Selumetinib is an orally bioavailable, non-ATP competitive kinase inhibitor of MEK1/2, upstream regulators of the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK pathway; in NF1 mouse models it inhibited ERK phosphorylation and reduced neurofibroma number, volume, and proliferation

rems.type: A REMS is not recommended for selumetinib given the current safety profile and the experience of the medical community in managing expected MEK inhibitor toxicities

advisory_committee.vote: The Division did not obtain the advice of the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee (ODAC); there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion

description.text: Removed the fasting restriction from dosing instructions and updated food effects and duration of response data

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for updates to the US Prescribing Information labeling by removing the fasting restriction from Section 2.1, (Dosing and Administration, Recommended Dosage), to update Section 12.3 with results from food effects studies, and to update duration of response data for SPRINT Phase II Stratum 1 (Section 14, Clinical Studies).

description.text: Expanded to include pediatric patients 1 year of age and older with NF1 who have symptomatic, inoperable plexiform neurofibromas

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the use of Kosalugo to treat pediatric patients 1 year of age and older with neurofibromatosis type 1 who have symptomatic, inoperable plexiform neurofibromas.

description.text: Expanded indication to include adult patients (age 1 year and older) with NF1 and symptomatic, inoperable plexiform neurofibromas

basis.text: Breakthrough Therapy Designation granted March 29, 2019; the primary data supporting the BTD request came from 50 patients enrolled in SPRINT Phase 2, Stratum 1

citations.quote: On March 29, 2019, the FDA granted BTD to selumetinib for the treatment of pediatric patients aged 3 years and above, with NF1 and inoperable PN that is causing significant morbidity.
The primary data supporting the BTD request for selumetinib came from 50 patients enrolled in SPRINT Phase 2, stratum 1.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan Product Designation for the treatment of NF1, granted February 2018

citations.quote: The drug was granted Orphan Product Designation for the treatment of NF1 in February 2018, and Breakthrough Therapy Designation was granted in March 2019.

summary.text: Selumetinib received Orphan Drug Designation (Feb 2018) and Breakthrough Therapy Designation (Mar 2019), and the NDA was granted Priority review. It was approved by regular (not accelerated) approval based on a durable ORR in the single-arm SPRINT Phase II Stratum 1 trial.

citations.quote: The drug was granted Orphan Product Designation for the treatment of NF1 in February 2018, and Breakthrough Therapy Designation was granted in March 2019.
These factors represent direct clinical benefit to patients and warrant regular approval of the dr

requirement.text: 3806-1: Characterize and evaluate the long-term safety effects and potential for serious adverse risks of selumetinib on growth and development of pediatric patients; submit final report and long-term follow-up data from SPRINT and other studies

citations.quote: 3806-1 Characterize and evaluate the long-term safety effects and any potential for serious adverse risks of selumetinib on the growth and development of pediatric patients. Submit the complete final report and long-term follow-up data from pediatric patients enrolled on SPRINT and ongoing or completed studies of selumetinib.

requirement.text: 3806-2: Characterize and evaluate long-term safety effects and specific serious adverse risks (ocular, cardiac, muscle, GI, dermatologic toxicity) in pediatric patients; submit final report and ≥ 7 years follow-up safety data

citations.quote: Characterize and evaluate the long-term safety effects and any potential for specific serious adverse risks of selumetinib in pediatric patients. Submit the complete final report and long-term follow-up safety data (minimum of 7 years) from pediatric patients enrolled on SPRINT and all other ongoing or completed studies of selumetinib

requirement.text: 3806-3: Submit final report and datasets from a pharmacokinetic trial in pediatric patients to confirm the effect of a low-fat meal on selumetinib exposure with the marketed capsule formulation and confirm appropriate dosing with a low-fat meal

citations.quote: Submit the final report and datasets from a pharmacokinetic trial in pediatric patients to confirm the effect of a low-fat meal on selumetinib exposure with the marketed capsule formulation and evaluate whether administration of selumetinib with food may alleviate gastrointestinal toxicities. Confirm appropriate dosing recommendation of selumetinib with a low-fat meal that maintains efficacy with acceptable safety.
